title: Explicit task workspaces with canonical workflow state
outcomes: Manage one task worktree with explicit owner/run/base and retain the canonical .go control state.

in: Workspace create/reuse/recovery, canonical state resolution, execution/integration locks, full-diff scope checks and cleanup gates
out: Release publisher, autonomous active-task resume and project service/database isolation
boundaries: Canonical .go control state, Git common directory and registered task worktree

decision_rights: Authorize execution and choose model; GO on 2026-09-13
Implement bounded contract choices and document compatibility behavior

constraints: Require explicit workspace path, branch, base branch and base commit; do not guess main/master.
Registry lives in canonical .go; per-worktree Git metadata identifies its control root. Copied workflow queues are not authoritative.
A matching active task claim owns each workspace; reuse requires the same owner/run and Git identity.
Hold execution/integration locks across the operation; retain work on conflicts, dirty state, unproven release or cleanup failures.
Expose workspace primitives now; fresh-worker and active-task orchestration follows in abc-03/04.

quality_attributes.scenario: Duplicate create, changed owner/run or interrupted create
CLI invoked in a registered linked worktree
Committed out-of-scope work, canonical user dirt or unproven delivery

risks: A worktree isolates Git state; project ports/databases and a security sandbox require separate explicit policies.
